Von Neumann hierarchy (Vα​)

Words: 45 Articles: 1
Set theory OurBigBook.com
The von Neumann hierarchy is
V0​=∅,Vα+1​=P(Vα​),Vλ​=⋃β<λ​Vβ​.
(1)
Every level is transitive, the levels are increasing, and every set belongs to some level.

Rank of a set

Words: 19
Von Neumann hierarchy OurBigBook.com
The rank is defined by
rank(x)=supy∈x​(rank(y)+1).
(2)
It is the least ordinal α for which x⊆Vα​.

Transitive set

Words: 20
Set theory OurBigBook.com
A set X is transitive when every element of an element of X is itself an element of X.

Well-founded relation

Words: 23
Set theory OurBigBook.com
A relation r on X is well-founded when every nonempty subset of X contains an element with no r-predecessor in that subset.

Extensional relation

Words: 12
Set theory OurBigBook.com
A relation is extensional when distinct elements have distinct sets of predecessors.

Set

Words: 243 Articles: 17
Set theory OurBigBook.com
A set is a collection of distinct objects regarded as its elements.

Empty set (∅)

Words: 6
Set OurBigBook.com
The empty set has no elements.

Singleton set

Words: 7
Set OurBigBook.com
A singleton set has exactly one element.

Distinct elements

Words: 7
Set OurBigBook.com
Elements are distinct when they are unequal.

Generating set

Words: 20
Set OurBigBook.com
A generating set is a subset from which every element of a structure can be obtained using the structure's operations.

Subset

Words: 17
Set OurBigBook.com
A set A is a subset of B when every element of A belongs to B.

Set union (⋃)

Words: 17
Set OurBigBook.com
The union ⋃i∈I​Ai​ contains exactly the elements that belong to at least one set Ai​.

Set intersection (⋂)

Words: 15
Set OurBigBook.com
The intersection ⋂i∈I​Ai​ contains exactly the elements that belong to every set Ai​.

Pair

Words: 22 Articles: 2
Set OurBigBook.com
A pair is a collection of two objects. An ordered pair records which object is first, whereas an unordered pair does not.
Ordered pair
Pair OurBigBook.com
Unordered pair
Pair OurBigBook.com

Partially ordered set

Words: 64 Articles: 2
Set OurBigBook.com
A partially ordered set, or poset, is a set equipped with a reflexive, antisymmetric and transitive binary relation.
Maximal element of a partially ordered set
Words: 30
Partially ordered set OurBigBook.com
An element m of a partially ordered set is maximal when m≤x implies x=m. A poset can have several maximal elements and need not have a greatest element.
Minimal element of a partially ordered set
Words: 16
Partially ordered set OurBigBook.com
An element m of a partially ordered set is minimal when x≤m implies x=m.

Total order

Words: 56 Articles: 3
Set OurBigBook.com
A total order is a reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive relation in which every two elements are comparable.
Empty order
Words: 11
Total order OurBigBook.com
The empty order is the unique total order on the empty set.
Greatest element
Words: 18
Total order OurBigBook.com
An element is greatest when every element of the ordered set is less than or equal to it.
Initial segment
Words: 11
Total order OurBigBook.com
An initial segment contains every element below each of its elements.

Binary relation

Words: 84 Articles: 4
Set theory OurBigBook.com
A binary relation on a set X is a subset of X×X.

Reflexive relation

Words: 17
Binary relation OurBigBook.com
A relation R on X is reflexive when xRx for every x∈X.

Symmetric relation

Words: 15
Binary relation OurBigBook.com
A relation R is symmetric when xRy implies yRx.

Transitive relation

Words: 19
Binary relation OurBigBook.com
A relation R is transitive when xRy and yRz imply xRz.

Equivalence relation

Words: 19
Binary relation OurBigBook.com
An equivalence relation is a reflexive, symmetric, and transitive binary relation. It partitions a set into disjoint equivalence classes.

Function

Words: 151 Articles: 9
Set theory OurBigBook.com
A function assigns exactly one output to each input in its domain.

Identity function (id)

Words: 13
Function OurBigBook.com
The identity function on a set X maps every x∈X to itself.

Piecewise-linear function

Words: 23
Function OurBigBook.com
A piecewise-linear function is linear on each member of a finite or locally finite partition of its domain into intervals or polyhedral pieces.

Bounded function

Words: 30 Articles: 1
Function OurBigBook.com
A real- or complex-valued function is bounded when the moduli of all its values have one finite upper bound.
Unbounded function
Words: 12
Bounded function OurBigBook.com
An unbounded function has no finite bound on the moduli of its values.

Constant function

Words: 10
Function OurBigBook.com
A constant function has the same output for every input.

Real-valued function

Words: 27 Articles: 1
Function OurBigBook.com
A real-valued function has codomain contained in the real numbers.
Global maximum
Words: 17
Real-valued function OurBigBook.com
A global maximum of a real-valued function is a value f(x0​) satisfying f(x)≤f(x0​) throughout its domain.

Bijection

Words: 19
Function OurBigBook.com
A bijection is a function that is both injective and surjective, so every target element has exactly one preimage.

Periodic function

Words: 17
Function OurBigBook.com
A function is periodic when f(x+T)=f(x) for some nonzero period T and every x in its domain.

Zorn lemma

Words: 20
Set theory OurBigBook.com
If every chain in a nonempty partially ordered set has an upper bound, then the set has a maximal element.

Class in set theory

Words: 164 Articles: 4
Set theory OurBigBook.com
A class is a collection of sets specified by a formula, possibly with set parameters. A class is a set when one set has exactly those members.

Proper class

Words: 14
Class in set theory OurBigBook.com
A proper class is a class in set theory that is not a set in the ambient universe.

Transitive class

Words: 123 Articles: 2
Class in set theory OurBigBook.com
A class M is transitive when x∈y∈M implies x∈M. Consequently, every member of a member of M is available as an element of the structure (M,∈).
Basic set-theoretic axioms inherited by a transitive class
Words: 48
Transitive class OurBigBook.com
If a transitive class M contains the empty set and is closed under pairing and union, then (M,∈) satisfies extensionality, empty set, pairing, and union. Transitivity makes all members of each x∈M visible inside M, so the ambient witnesses have the same required membership relations internally.
Formula relativization to a class
Words: 44
Transitive class OurBigBook.com
The relativization φM of a formula φ is obtained recursively by restricting every quantifier to M:
(∃xψ)M=∃x(x∈M∧ψM),(∀xψ)M=∀x(x∈M⇒ψM).
(3)
For parameters in M, the ambient statement φM holds exactly when the structure (M,∈) satisfies φ.

Axiom schema of replacement

Words: 27
Set theory OurBigBook.com
Every definable function-class maps a set-sized domain to a set-sized range. Functionality means that the defining formula assigns exactly one output to each input in the domain.

Axiom of foundation

Words: 54 Articles: 1
Set theory OurBigBook.com
Every nonempty set A has an element x∈A such that x∩A=∅.

Epsilon induction (∈-induction)

Words: 40
Axiom of foundation OurBigBook.com
The principle of epsilon induction says that every progressive class is universal: if
∀x[(∀y∈x, φ(y))⟹φ(x)],
(4)
then φ(x) holds for every set x. Over the other axioms of ZF, it is equivalent to the Axiom of foundation.

Axiom of power set

Words: 19
Set theory OurBigBook.com
For every set x there is a set P(x) whose members are exactly the subsets of x.

Words: 125 Articles: 4
Set theory OurBigBook.com
The cumulative hierarchy is defined by V0​=∅, Vα+1​=P(Vα​), and Vλ​=⋃α<λ​Vα​ at limit ordinals.

If the second coordinate of p restricted to the K-summand covers L, it is the required surjection. Otherwise choose l0​ that it misses. Every (k,l0​) then has its preimage in the L-summand.
